summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission after bone marrow transplant, anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 11%, chronic graft-versus-host disease, bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia, and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, was admitted for rectal pain and chills. He presented with hypotension and an elevated lactate, consistent with septic shock. Imaging revealed a new 5.4 cm perianal abscess, which was drained at the bedside by colorectal surgery. His infection resolved with source control, and antibiotics were discontinued. He had an episode of vomiting attributed to calcium acetate, which was switched to sevelamer. He remained stable on his home oxygen and continued his regular dialysis schedule. His condition improved, and he was discharged home with follow-up arranged, new medication instructions, and guidance on weight monitoring and symptom reporting.
